estimate.revisionNotifyPercent.authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(vii)(b), (a)(7)(B)(ii); OORC Schedule; Model Policy; Best Practices; FAQ (all searched)
estimate.revisionNotifyPercent.notes: Documented absence: no revision-percentage trigger. Indirect consequence only: the nonpayment bar (TN-9001) reaches only 'the estimated cost' the requestor agreed to, and no charge may be collected before an estimate (TN-9014) — so an overrun beyond the agreed estimate is unsupported unless a rev…

estimate.validityDays.label: Estimate validity period (days)
estimate.validityDays.authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503; OORC Schedule; Model Policy; Best Practices; Records Request/Response Forms; FAQ (all searched)
estimate.validityDays.notes: Documented absence: no expiry period for an estimate in statute or OORC guidance.

rules.deposit.threshold.label: Deposit / prepayment may be required above ($)
rules.deposit.threshold.unit: USD (entity fills in; prepayment permitted at any amount)
rules.deposit.threshold.authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.B, § VI.G; OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.E; Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(g)(1)(C)
rules.deposit.threshold.notes: State permits prepayment of the estimate at any amount and hands the threshold to the entity as a blank in the model policy; Best Practices § III.H (advisory) suggests prepayment 'when duplication costs ... are significant'. Statutory scope of the policy duty is county/municipal (§ 10-7-503(g)(1)).

rules.deposit.percent.label: Deposit capped at (% of estimate)
rules.deposit.percent.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.E; Model Policy § VI.B; Best Practices § III.H; Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503 (all searched)
rules.deposit.percent.notes: Documented absence of any cap: guidance expressly contemplates 'full or partial payment of estimated charges' before production, so 100% prepayment is permitted; no percentage ceiling anywhere. City sets any cap in policy.

payment.productionGate.label: Production may be conditioned on payment (pay before copies / pay in full before release)
payment.productionGate.value: prepay_permitted_before_production (full or partial prepayment of the itemized estimate; production may be withheld until paid; may be segmented with segmented production)
payment.productionGate.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.E; OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.B; OORC Records Response Form; Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(vii)(b)
payment.productionGate.notes: Permission, not requirement: the entity chooses whether to condition production on payment; when it does, the official response form recognizes non-payment of estimated fees as a ground for withholding. Post-production nonpayment triggers the future-request bar (TN-9001).

payment.nonpayment.label: Nonpayment consequence (withdrawn after N days; prior-debt prepayment)
payment.nonpayment.value: prior_debt_bar_until_paid (entity not required to comply with ANY further request from the person until unpaid copies are paid; conditioned on a prior estimate the person agreed to); no statutory N-day withdrawal
payment.nonpayment.authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(vii)(b); OORC FAQ 'Are there penalties for failing to inspect or pay for copies of public records?'
payment.nonpayment.notes: Applies to all governmental entities. The OORC FAQ (official) restates the clause verbatim and adds that where a requestor converts a copy request to inspection after copies were produced in reliance on an agreement, the entity 'may be entitled to seek equitable relief'. No withdrawal-after-N-day…

payment.depositClock.label: Statutory clock effect while a deposit is unpaid; grace; lapse action
payment.depositClock.value: hold: production withheld while required estimated fees are unpaid; no statutory clock effect, grace period or lapse action defined
payment.depositClock.authority: OORC Records Response Form; OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.E; Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(2)(B)
payment.depositClock.notes: Searched § 10-7-503(a)(2)–(3), (a)(7); Schedule; Model Policy; FAQ: nothing tolls, pauses or restarts the response clock for an unpaid deposit, and there is no grace period or automatic lapse/withdrawal. City sets grace/lapse in policy.

payment.reissue.label: Overrun re-issue rules (revised estimate required / blocks collection / restarts window)
payment.reissue.value: collection blocked until an estimate has been provided; nonpayment bar reaches only the estimate the requestor agreed to; no explicit revised-estimate rule and no window restart
payment.reissue.authority: OORC FAQ (applying Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)(ii)); Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(vii)(b)
payment.reissue.notes: Overrun handling is left to the city; the state's only constraints are the estimate-before-charge rule and the agreed-estimate condition on the nonpayment bar.

rules.maxFee.label: Request-level ceiling (actual cost cap / statutory max)
rules.maxFee.value: “reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material” — no request-level dollar cap; per-page ceilings under the schedule; anything above requires documented actual cost; excessive fees shall not hinder access
rules.maxFee.authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)(i); § 8-4-604(a)(1)(A)(ii)(b); OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.C, § II.C
rules.maxFee.notes: The operative standard is 'reasonable costs incurred in producing' assessed per the OORC manner; the safe harbor makes schedule-consistent fees presumptively reasonable; unreasonable/unfounded costs can be treated as a denial reviewable under § 10-7-505 (OORC FAQ).

rules.deMinimis.label: De-minimis: no charge below ($)
rules.deMinimis.authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.E, § VI.C; OORC Best Practices § III.G; Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(g)(1)(C)
rules.deMinimis.notes: State sets no de-minimis floor; the model policy offers two blanks (no-charge below $/pages; discretionary waiver below $) for the entity to fill.

rules.minFee.label: Minimum fee
rules.minFee.unit: USD (entity determines from its administrative cost)
rules.minFee.authority: OORC Best Practices & Guidelines § III.G; Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(g)(1)(C)
rules.minFee.notes: No statewide minimum fee found in § 10-7-503, § 8-4-604, the Schedule, Model Policy or FAQ.

media.label: Electronic media (CD/DVD/USB) charge
media.value: “actual out-of-pocket costs for flash drives or similar storage devices”
media.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § III.B
media.notes: No fixed CD/DVD/USB figure; pass-through of actual device cost only. Model Policy § V.D lets the entity decide whether requestor-supplied storage devices are accepted (Best Practices flags security concerns).

delivery.label: Delivery: mail / handling / email / pickup
delivery.value: “actual cost of delivering the copies” (USPS First-Class Mail obligatory once paid/waived; other means incl. electronic at custodian's discretion and cost)
delivery.unit: USD, actual cost (postage); no handling fee
delivery.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § III.C–D; OORC Model Public Records Policy § V.B–C; OORC FAQ
delivery.notes: Pickup presumed (§ III.C); mail at actual cost after payment; email/electronic delivery discretionary — no state figure for any channel; no handling surcharge authorized.

certification.label: Certification / certified-copy charge
certification.authority: Tenn. Code Ann. §§ 10-7-503, 10-7-506, 8-4-604; OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges; Model Public Records Policy; Best Practices; FAQ; Tenn. Code Ann. § 6-54-120(a)(1)(D) (municipal recorder duty to certify copies, no fee stated) — all searched
certification.notes: Documented absence for TPRA copies: neither the statute nor any OORC instrument sets a certified-copy charge; § 6-54-120 lists 'certifying copies of official records' as a recorder duty without a fee.

av.label: Audio/video: per recording, per minute, free minutes
av.value: documented “actual cost” for records produced on a medium other than standard paper; storage device at actual out-of-pocket cost; labor per § IV — no per-recording / per-minute figure and no free-minutes rule
av.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.C, § III.B, § IV
av.notes: Searched Schedule, Model Policy, FAQ, § 10-7-503: no per-recording, per-minute or free-minutes rule.

commercial.label: Commercial-purpose schedule (surcharge %, labor becomes chargeable)
commercial.unit: % of total development costs recoverable as an ADDITIONAL fee for commercial-value GIS/geographic-data reproductions only; general records: no purpose-based surcharge and labor chargeability does not change
commercial.authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-506(c)(1), (3), (4); OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.F
commercial.notes: Two-part answer: (1) general records — no commercial schedule (Schedule § I.F); (2) commercial-value computer-generated maps/geographic data developed with public funds — additional reasonable fees for development cost recovery, capped at 10% (20% with approvals), not chargeable to individuals fo…

waiver.label: Fee waiver: grounds, mandatory vs discretionary, purpose statement, written denial, appeal
waiver.value: discretionary waiver/reduction 'in whole or in part, in accordance with the governmental entity's public records policy'; no statutory grounds, purpose statement, written-denial or appeal requirement
waiver.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.D; OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.C; OORC Best Practices § III.C
waiver.notes: Mandatory-vs-discretionary: discretionary; grounds: entity's policy (Best Practices suggests number of copies, dollar amount, record type/accessibility, public-interest dissemination); purpose statement: none required (TPRA does not distinguish by purpose); written denial/appeal: none in state la…

waiver.forfeiture.label: Late response forfeits the fee
waiver.forfeiture.authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(2)–(3), (a)(7); § 10-7-505; OORC Schedule; Model Policy; FAQ (all searched)
waiver.forfeiture.notes: Documented absence: a late/no response is a deemed denial with a court remedy; nothing in statute or OORC guidance forfeits or reduces the fee for a late response.

repeat.label: Repeat / aggregated requests (carry-forward, aggregation threshold)
repeat.unit: requests per calendar month (aggregation trigger; entity sets the number at or above 4 in its policy; optional to aggregate)
repeat.authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests §§ I.B–E, II.A–D (delegated from Tenn. Code Ann. § 8-4-604(a)(2))
repeat.notes: No carry-forward/estimate-reuse rule for repeat requests; the state mechanism is aggregation: single requestor or multiple requestors acting in concert (coordinator determination), threshold ≥4/month set by policy, level (entity/department) set by policy, effect = free hour and other per-request …

fee.copy_rate_per_page.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.A
fee.copy_rate_per_page.summary: For each standard 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 black-and-white copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per-page charge of up to 15 cents ($0.15).

fee.labor_charge.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § IV.C
fee.labor_charge.summary: The labor threshold is the first (1st) hour of labor reasonably necessary to produce requested material; a governmental entity may adopt a higher threshold, and labor may be charged only for time exceeding the threshold.

fee.labor_charge.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges §§ IV.B, IV.D, IV.E
fee.labor_charge.summary: Labor above the threshold is charged at the hourly wage of the employee(s) reasonably necessary, using the lowest practicable wage; the hourly wage is the employee's base salary (excluding benefits), computed by dividing annual salary by required hours per year.

fee.actual_cost_basis.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § III.A
fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: When assessing fees for copies, records custodians shall utilize the most economical and efficient method of producing the requested records.

fee.actual_cost_basis.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.C
fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: If actual costs are higher than the schedule amounts, or records are produced on a non-standard medium, the entity may develop its own charges but must document 'actual cost' calculation and reasoning in an adopted policy; charges above $0.15 (B&W) / $0.50 (color) require documented actual-cost a…

fee.electronic_media_charge.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges §§ III.B, III.E, III.F
fee.electronic_media_charge.summary: A custodian may charge actual out-of-pocket cost for flash drives/storage devices provided; if internal production is not practicable, may use an outside vendor and charge those actual costs; and may recover actual retrieval charges assessed by an archive or other entity holding the records.

fee.nonstandard_rate.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.A
fee.nonstandard_rate.summary: For each standard 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 color copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per-page charge of up to 50 cents ($0.50).

fee.commercial_charge.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.F, citing Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-506(c)
fee.commercial_charge.summary: Although standard copy/labor charges do not vary by purpose, other statutory provisions (e.g., § 10-7-506(c)) enumerate fees that may be assessed when specific documents are requested for a specific use.

fee.schedule_and_authority.summary: A records custodian may require a requestor to pay the custodian's reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material, assessed in the manner established by the Office of Open Records Counsel pursuant to § 8-4-604.

classification.written_policy_required.summary: Every county and municipal governmental entity shall establish a written public records policy, adopted by its governing authority, that is not more burdensome than state law and includes the request process and any required form, the response process (including redaction), a statement of fees an…

fee.schedule_and_authority.summary: A records custodian may require a requestor to pay the custodian's reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material, assessed in the manner established by the Office of Open Records Counsel pursuant to § 8-4-604.

fee.aggregation.authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.D
fee.aggregation.summary: A governmental entity's policy shall specify the number of requests within a calendar month that triggers aggregation; that amount must be no lower than four (4) requests.

fee.aggregation.authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § II.A
fee.aggregation.summary: Once a records custodian reaches the aggregation threshold, the custodian is no longer required to deduct the labor threshold or any other minimum charge per request that would ordinarily be waived.

fee.aggregation.authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.C
fee.aggregation.summary: An entity may aggregate multiple requests by a single requestor, and may aggregate requests by multiple requestors if the coordinator determines they are acting in concert with each other or as agents of another person, entity, or organization.

payment.advance_payment.authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.E; Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)
payment.advance_payment.summary: A records custodian may require payment for copies before producing the copies of the records.
